solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What about country female becoming a bitch?

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: 'Eh?' is an exclamation meaning 'what?'
the Caribbean island nation

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about some country woman who turns nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitch' is literal here, not an insult: in Greek myth the Trojan queen was turned into a dog after Troy fell.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend Priam's widow was transformed into a female dog after the fall of Troy, so she is a woman who became a bitch.

clue.text: Laugh about woman getting cold — and what comes with it?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the laugh goes round the other pieces

parts.note: 'he-he' is a written laugh
Ada is a woman's name
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone laughs at a woman catching a cold and asks what symptom follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the cold in the clue: a sore head is a common companion of a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain in the head is a typical symptom accompanying a cold, so it is what comes with one.

clue.text: It's hard being old-fashioned

definitions.meaning: in an old sense the word means hard and horny, like a corn on the foot

explanation.surface: A complaint that being out of date is a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the rare one: having corns, or horny like a corn.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday sense is hackneyed or dated, as with a stale joke; the rarer sense means horny-skinned and tough.

clue.text: Twisted male governed

parts.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit
led means directed or ruled

explanation.surface: A warped man held power.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that has bent out of shape under pressure is warped or distorted.

clue.text: Give the most convincing cry of pain?

parts.note: best means the most convincing or finest
'ow!' is what you cry when hurt

explanation.surface: Asking someone to produce their most believable yelp of agony.
explanation.definitionFit: To confer or present something, such as an honour, is to grant it.

clue.text: Always abiding with outward sign of love invisible

indicators.note: invisible means the kiss is not to be seen, so it drops out

parts.note: outward means on the outside, exterior
a kiss, written as X at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Undying love that needs no outward show to prove it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invisible' removes the X (a kiss) from the word for outward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting endures for all time, abiding always.

clue.text: You were spotted by eavesdropper, we hear — lad seeking adventure

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are spoken, in a slangy accent

parts.note: a Peeping Tom spied you: 'Tom saw you', with 'you' said colloquially as 'yer'

explanation.surface: Someone warns you that a snoop caught sight of you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' asks for the phrase as it sounds: 'Tom saw yer'. A Peeping Tom is a voyeur, loosely an eavesdropper.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's boy hero is a youngster whose story is full of escapades along the Mississippi.

clue.text: Manipulate piece of laundry equipment, inverting piece at the top

indicators.note: turning the top letter upside down changes an M into a W

parts.note: a mangle is a roller wringer for pressing water out of washing

explanation.surface: Instructions for fiddling with a household wringer by flipping its top part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverting piece at the top': in a down entry the first letter is the top, and an M turned upside down looks like a W.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer an outcome by crafty means is to fix or finagle it.

clue.text: Protests loudly against large ugly buildings?

definitions.meaning: to jeer or heckle, as a crowd does a team
soldiers' quarters, and by extension any big bleak block

explanation.surface: Someone shouts objections to the construction of grim, oversized buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means jeering or heckling; the noun is military housing, often used of any big plain block.

clue.text: Paths strewn with misery? I could be the answer!

definitions.text: Paths strewn with misery? I could be the answer!

indicators.note: strewn means scattered about, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone whose road through life is full of sorrow; the speaker offers to be the remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strewn' scatters PATHS and MISERY together; 'with' just joins them. The whole clue also describes one offering comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who feels compassion is the person to answer a life full of suffering with support.

clue.text: What suits lord or monarch — source of wealth

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a mine yields gold or coal, a rich source

explanation.surface: Asking what clothing befits a peer or a king, and where riches come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is only a link between the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The white winter fur of the stoat trims peers' ceremonial robes, so it is fitting dress for a nobleman.

clue.text: Female overweight must lose a bit in the middle

indicators.text: must lose a bit in the middle
indicators.note: the central letter of the word is to be dropped

parts.note: lardy is an informal word for fat

explanation.surface: A heavy woman needs to slim her waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose a bit in the middle' removes the R, the central letter of the five.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman, especially a polite or well-born one, is a female person.

clue.text: Awful food given to the French servants

indicators.note: given to means the food is attached after the other pieces

parts.note: la is French for 'the' (feminine)
men are attendants or servants
table can mean the food served, as in 'a good table'

explanation.surface: A complaint about the dreadful meals served to French domestic staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'table' in the sense of fare served, as in 'keeps a fine table'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deplorable or regrettable things are dreadful, deserving to be mourned.

clue.text: Mature version of cricketer and commentator in court?

definitions.text: Mature version of cricketer and commentator in court?

parts.words: Mature version of cricketer and commentator in court
parts.note: Trevor Bailey was an England cricketer and later radio commentator; an aged version of him would be an old Bailey, which is also London's chief criminal court

explanation.surface: A query about an older form of a famous player turned broadcaster appearing before judges.
explanation.walkthrough: Trevor Bailey played cricket for England and commentated on BBC radio; London's Central Criminal Court is popularly named after its street.
explanation.definitionFit: The popular name of London's Central Criminal Court, where major trials are held.

clue.text: One composer bringing endless distress to another

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: to offend is to upset or distress
another composer: J S Bach

explanation.surface: A musician causing perpetual torment to a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing ... to' just sets the shortened verb before the second composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Offenbach wrote operettas such as Orpheus in the Underworld, so he is a composer.

clue.text: Text from old politician, revolutionary beast making a splash?

parts.note: LIB is a Liberal, from the old British Liberal Party

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the animal is written backwards

parts.note: an otter is a water-loving animal

explanation.surface: Writings by a former party member about a radical sensation-seeking brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses OTTER to RETTO.
explanation.definitionFit: The words of an opera or musical are its script, the text sung.

clue.text: Achievement with plant by the wet flibbertigibbet

parts.note: a feat is an accomplishment
a herb is a plant
rain is the wet weather

explanation.surface: A scatty person's triumph of growing something out in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'by' just join the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A silly, flighty person is a scatterbrain, someone with no sense.

clue.text: Lab involved with mice still

indicators.note: involved means mixed up together, so the letters are combined and rearranged

explanation.surface: A laboratory is still mixed up with experiments on rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb but is the noun: distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: This old distilling apparatus is a kind of still, used by alchemists.

clue.text: Comic hero and friend sparing no expense?

parts.note: Roy of the Rovers, footballer hero of a long-running British boys' comic strip
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A cartoon champion and his pal spending lavishly.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy Race of 'Roy of the Rovers' was a British comic-strip footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things in a kingly manner means lavishly, splendidly and without stinting.

clue.text: Animal, the thing with one foot for climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: it refers to a thing
I is the Roman numeral one
an animal's foot is a paw

explanation.surface: A creature with a single limb adapted for scaling heights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for climbing' reverses ITIPAW, reading it upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The North American elk is a large deer, so a kind of animal.

clue.text: How Spain turns into Sweden briefly without any trouble

definitions.text: How Spain turns into Sweden briefly without any trouble

indicators.note: the country turns into a shorter word when the Swedish letter is dropped from it

parts.note: the country, written as is
S is the international abbreviation for Sweden
-less is the suffix meaning without
-ly is the suffix that turns a word into an adverb of manner, answering 'how?'

explanation.surface: Asking how one country could be transformed into another with no fuss at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns into' drops S (Sweden) from SPAIN to leave PAIN; 'without' adds LESS and 'How' the adverb ending LY, while the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with no hurt or difficulty is doing it easily, free of trouble.

clue.text: Type of good person protecting soldiers

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping around, so the saint encloses the soldiers

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a good person
OR is Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A kind of decent person who looks after troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind or category of thing is its variety or class.

clue.text: Foreign character's scar dermatologist finally removed

indicators.note: removed means the letter is taken out

parts.note: a stigma is a mark or scar

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A skin specialist got rid of someone's strange-looking scar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives T, the last letter of 'dermatologist', which 'removed' takes out.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet is a letter from a foreign script.

clue.text: One vehicle covered in very black powder

indicators.note: covered in means enclosed, so the other pieces sit inside

parts.note: BB is the pencil grade for very black lead
I is the Roman numeral one
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A single car coated in jet-black dust.
explanation.walkthrough: BB marks a very soft, very black pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium bicarbonate, used in baking, is a white powder known by this short name.

clue.text: Hesitation about diplomat lower in status

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the hesitation is read backwards

parts.note: 'er' is a sound of hesitation
a legate is an envoy, such as a papal ambassador

explanation.surface: An envoy is demoted after dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: A legate is a papal envoy; 'about' signals reading the hesitation backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To demote something, as a football club to a lower division, is to downgrade it.

clue.text: Italian journalist is cut off near a Greek island

parts.note: IT is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

indicators.note: cut off means the last letter is chopped

parts.note: a hack is a journalist

explanation.surface: An Italian reporter is stranded close to an island in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' just places A beside the trimmed HACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus's home is an island in the Ionian Sea off western Greece.

clue.text: Energetic person has Monday working

indicators.note: working means in operation, so the letters of the weekday are set to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A go-getter is back at the job at the start of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirelessly lively person is likened to the electrical generator, a powerhouse.
